contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-pay-by-bank-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank/accept-a-payment`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank/accept-a-payment lists Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API, plus iOS and Android (new raw lines 5-19). Those links establish documentation routes. The May 6, 2026 guide covers single-use, bank-authenticated redirect payments through Checkout and web Elements PaymentIntents. Checkout lists payment mode, same-currency single-purchase line items, DE/GB business locations and EUR/GBP, with a GBP-specific manual instruction. Manual Checkout sets `pay_by_bank` and a statement descriptor, with `success_url` in hosted and `return_url` in full embedded examples (old raw lines 12-112). Web Elements uses a server-priced PaymentIntent, client-secret handoff, client `confirmPayment` with `return_url`, and PaymentIntent status retrieval (old raw lines 156-200 and old raw lines 419-450). The May guide describes immediate success/failure notification specifically for Pay by Bank (old raw lines 12-18 and old raw lines 135-141). Its generic Elements examples handle `succeeded`, `processing` and `requires_payment_method` without establishing a Pay by Bank-specific transition or timing (old raw lines 515-569 and old raw lines 587-624). Bank authorization and browser return do not establish verified success, available funds, or payout. source-stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment.md summarizes the May routes but generalizes the descriptor and geography and lacks the November navigation leaves.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank/accept-a-payment, the November replacement is a navigation change, including an explicit Elements API split and two mobile links (new raw lines 9-19 versus old raw lines 8-10, old raw lines 135-141 and old raw lines 156-196). The index establishes no SDK contract, current eligibility, or substantive API change. Keep May's one-time Checkout eligibility, manual Checkout statement descriptor, UI-specific return fields, server/client and status boundaries, test steps, and qualified refund timing dated in source-stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment.md (old raw lines 20-127, old raw lines 156-200, old raw lines 269-318, old raw lines 515-569 and old raw lines 632-634). Maintain reciprocal warnings for the May compatibility table versus GBP-only instruction, DE/GB business versus France/Germany/Ireland preview wording, and the inconsistent Swish and USD Dashboard example (old raw lines 20-49 and old raw lines 160-196). The May immediate-notification statement (old raw lines 12-18 and old raw lines 135-141) disagrees with the April 20, 2026 Dashboard-managed Checkout migration guide, which includes Pay by Bank in its delayed-notification list (raw/stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods-2025.md:66-84). Link the dated disagreement reciprocally and preserve the April advice to wait for verified success or failure when Checkout completion represents bank authorization. The general 2–14 day figure is not a method-specific promise. Keep customer return, verified success, funds availability and payout distinct. The separate November method overview describes `payment_method_provider_timeout` when funds fail to arrive in time after authorization and automatic return of late funds after failure (raw/stripe-payments-pay-by-bank-2026-11-07.md:260-264). The separate real-time product matrix's dated mobile-support change and method overview's Bacs-backed recurring private preview have their own evidence. Neither is established by the index, and the distinct preview does not change May Checkout subscription mode.
